bbc.title: Three die in Mexico City World Cup celebrations
bbc.description: More than one million people took to the streets of Mexico City on Tuesday to mark the country's win over Ecuador.

bbc.description: The president's crypto income far outpaces his earnings from real estate and Trump-themed items such as watches.

bbc.description: A man is seen clambering through a window to escape black smoke in the block where some 200 people live.

bbc.description: The collision left holes on the side of the tower, but Beijing has scrubbed other visible traces of the incident.

bbc.description: Video footage shows rescuers cheering as the child is pulled from rubble in La Guaira state.

bbc.title: Canada will take part in Eurovision Song Contest 2027
bbc.description: The country becomes the first new participant since Australia joined the contest in 2015.

bbc.title: US Supreme Court upholds birthright citizenship in blow to Trump
bbc.description: The ruling is a major setback for Donald Trump's immigration agenda, and has been welcomed by civil rights groups.

bbc.title: Sudan's RSF committed crimes against humanity in el-Fasher, Amnesty says
bbc.description: The Amnesty report adds to evidence of atrocities in el-Fasher, which the UN says bore the hallmarks of genocide.

bbc.title: Afghan Taliban launch strikes on border with Pakistan as tensions escalate
bbc.description: Pakistan's military says it shot down four rudimentary drones and will respond to any further provocation.

bbc.title: Anthropic says US lifts export ban on its advanced AI tools
bbc.description: Fable and Mythos were abruptly suspended in June over concerns that they could be used by hackers.

bbc.title: US envoys in Doha to meet mediators but not Iranians, Qatar says
bbc.description: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman says no high-level meetings or direct talks between the US and Iran are scheduled.

bbc.title: Roof collapse kills 14 children at Pakistan tuition centre
bbc.description: Two people are taken into custody after the incident in the Kahna suburb of Lahore.

bbc.title: Firefighters struggle to contain deadly Greek wildfire
bbc.description: More than 100 firefighters are fighting a fire near Thessaloniki which has claimed at least two lives.

bbc.title: 'Absolute madness': Row over plan to demolish Nazi bunker under Berlin
bbc.description: City officials want to build flats on the city centre site but others say it should be preserved as part of Germany's history.

bbc.title: Thousands of anti-migrant protesters march in South Africa amid heavy police presence
bbc.description: Foreigners have already left South Africa ahead of the deadline set by anti-migrant groups.

bbc.title: US Supreme Court upholds bans on transgender athletes in female school and college sports
bbc.description: President Trump called the ruling a "big win", while an LGBT group said it was "heartbreaking".

bbc.title: US Supreme Court has dealt heavy defeats to Trump, while expanding his power
bbc.description: The birthright ruling brings to an end a Supreme Court term that has delivered the president some key victories.

bbc.title: Aftershock frays nerves as many Venezuelans left to fend for themselves
bbc.description: In areas devastated by the twin earthquakes, people are using crowbars, pickaxes and their bare hands to try to reach survivors.

euronews.title: Finnish entrepreneur jailed for breach of EU sanctions after exporting trucks to Russia
euronews.description: Finland's 1,340-kilometre border with Russia has been closed since December 2023 after the arrival of around 1,000 migrants without visas.

euronews.title: Just a few social media posts from self-styled 'experts' can strongly influence opinion, study says
euronews.description: Researchers warn social media users can form strong opinions after viewing only a few social media posts on a topic. Across social media, many self-proclaimed experts and influencers are plugging a gap amid declining public trust in traditional experts.

euronews.title: O Canada! Eurovision Song Contest welcomes first new country since 2015
euronews.description: Canada will sing at next Eurovision Song Contest after the country's public broadcaster confirmed full membership of the European Broadcasting Union - allowing them to compete in the world's biggest competition of its kind.

euronews.title: Mattel releases new Barbie in partnership with Miley Cyrus
euronews.description: Mattel releases yet another celebrity Barbie - this time with the American singer-songwriter and actress Miley Cyrus.

euronews.title: Ukraine hits Russia's Ufa oil refinery for second time in a week, Zelenskyy says
euronews.description: Ukraine’s domestically developed and manufactured drones and missiles have been hammering Russian oil facilities, including refineries, terminals, storage depots and pipeline pumping stations, for months.

euronews.title: Venice Romance: Andrea Bocelli celebrates 30th album anniversary with concert at Piazza San Marco
euronews.description: From crossover classics to stunning special guests, the Italian opera star Andrea Bocelli has left Venice swooning after an amazing show in celebration of the 30th anniversary of his pioneering album Romanza

euronews.title: Tourist takes lost Sorolla painting from Seville to Murcia: 'I thought it was a cool frame'
euronews.description: A tourist took home from Seville a painting left in the street while its owners loaded their car, then called police after realising the Valencian artist’s work was on a wanted list.

euronews.title: Ireland 'ambitious' to open more negotiation chapters with Ukraine during EU presidency
euronews.description: Ireland's Minister of State for European Affairs and Defence, Thomas Byrne, said the country's six-month EU presidency will be a "generational moment" with key priorities, including opening more negotiation clusters with Ukraine and strengthening the EU's economy.

euronews.title: Mourners attend funerals for 14 Pakistani children killed in tutoring centre roof collapse
euronews.description: Police are investigating whether negligence during ongoing construction work caused the collapse that left another eight children hospitalised in stable condition.

euronews.title: How this country is adopting AI in schools
euronews.description: Kazakhstan is turning to artificial intelligence to narrow educational disparities and reduce the teachers’ administrative workload - as part of a broader drive to build a digital economy.

euronews.title: EPP pushes to soften EU carbon market reforms in bid to shield industry
euronews.description: The largest political group in the European Parliament has urged the Commission to extend free carbon allowances for some industry sectors beyond 2030, according to a document seen by Euronews.

euronews.title: Health ministry changes conditions for resident doctors in framework statute reform
euronews.description: The draft bill, widely criticised across the sector and still awaiting approval in Congress, offers limited improvements for students. The MIR Spain Association acknowledges progress but deems the measures inadequate.

euronews.title: Google ordered to pay Klarna's PriceRunner €1.7 billion over search abuse
euronews.description: A Swedish court has ordered Google to pay 14.3 billion Swedish kronor plus interest (€1.7bn) in damages to PriceRunner, the price-comparison service owned by fintech group Klarna, ruling that the technology giant unlawfully favoured its own shopping service for years.

euronews.title: 'Bruising' film about OpenAI picked up by indie studio after Amazon snub
euronews.description: Neon has bought Luca Guadagnino's unflinching drama about Sam Altman, weeks after Amazon walked away from the nearly finished film following its $50 billion tie-up with OpenAI.

euronews.title: Two dead after storms batter Austria and Romania
euronews.description: Bucharest was hit particularly hard by storms overnight, with flooding damaging buildings and vehicles across the capital.

euronews.title: Ship runs aground in Hormuz as Iran insists on controlling the strait
euronews.description: Iran's IRGC said the grounding was caused by the vessel straying from its approved corridor. Hormuz control and the Israeli intervention against Hezbollah in Lebanon remain the two main obstacles to a final deal.

euronews.title: Water cannons cool tourists at Rome's Colosseum amid heatwave
euronews.description: Tourists at Rome's Colosseum cool off with water spray and bottled water as civil protection teams respond to temperatures approaching 40C.

euronews.title: At least six dead after blaze breaks out at Antwerp apartment block, police say
euronews.description: Antwerp police said the fire was caused by a "technical fault on the ground floor". The force has warned locals affected by the smoke to close windows and doors and to shut off ventilation systems if necessary.

rfi.title: Sudan's RSF accused of crimes against humanity in El Fasher
rfi.description: Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing while deliberately targeting children during their campaign to seize El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur state, Amnesty International said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Mali's war on civilians deepens as alliances shift, HRW says
rfi.description: Human Rights Watch (HRW) says the army, allied militias and Islamist armed groups have all committed abuses with impunity since the attacks in northern Mali in April.

rfi.title: Thousands rush to get tickets for Bayeux Tapestry's UK show
rfi.description: Thousands rushed to get tickets Wednesday for the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London, with the 11th-century artwork depicting the 1066 Norman conquest of England set to be transported from France for its first showing in the UK.

rfi.title: South Africa protesters confront migrant homes during nationwide marches
rfi.description: Protesters stopped outside buildings believed to house undocumented migrants and urged residents to leave as thousands marched across South Africa on Tuesday, the deadline set by anti-immigration groups for foreigners without papers to leave the country.

rfi.title: World's oceans record hottest June ever as new El Nino takes hold
rfi.description: The world's oceans reached their hottest June on record, scientists said on Wednesday, with sea temperatures expected to climb further as El Nino develops alongside human-driven climate change.

rfi.title: Ireland takes over EU presidency with French naval help on security
rfi.description: Ireland takes over the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union on Wednesday with French and British military assets expected to help protect a six-month programme of high-level meetings, as Dublin prepares for what security officials describe as an unusually demanding operation.

rfi.title: French justice system to re-examine 88,000 child abuse claims
rfi.description: Some 88,000 complaints regarding sexual violence against children are being re-examined by investigative services – a figure higher than the 70,000 initially ordered by Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin last month. This comes in the wake of the murder of 11-year-old Lyhanna, whose death prompted public outrage over the state's mishandling of child abuse cases.

rfi.title: Mbappe scores twice as France breeze past Sweden into World Cup last 16
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappe scored twice and Michael Olise was in scintillating form as France beat Sweden 3-0 at the World Cup on Tuesday and set up a last-16 clash with Paraguay.

rfi.title: Volvic to appeal after French court rules green claims were misleading
rfi.description: The bottled water brand Volvic has been found guilty of “misleading commercial practices” by the Paris Commercial Court over environmental claims made on its mineral water bottles, including that they were “carbon neutral” or “100 percent recyclable”.

rfi.title: Anti-independence parties make gains in New Caledonia provincial poll
rfi.description: New Caledonia’s non-independence parties gained ground in provincial elections on Sunday, according to provisional results, in a vote expected to shape the next round of talks with France over the Pacific territory’s future status.

rfi.title: South Africa braces for violence as anti-migrant marches reach boiling point
rfi.description: South African police were deployed in force across the country on Tuesday to forestall unrest and protests, as anti-immigrant groups' unofficial deadline for undocumented foreign nationals to leave the country fell. It follows a weeks-long campaign that has sent thousands fleeing and claimed four lives.

rfi.title: Uganda dissidents on trial as president’s son tightens control
rfi.description: Uganda's army chief, General Kainerugaba, has ordered the arrest of leading activists and politicians in recent weeks, and this weekend shut down the country's main independent media group. Two of those arrested appear in court this Tuesday: opposition figure Kizza Besigye and his lawyer.

rfi.title: French journalist Gleizes marks one year in Algerian prison as RSF renews appeal
rfi.description: French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes has now spent a year in detention in Algeria, prompting fresh calls from Reporters Without Borders and his family for his immediate release and a presidential pardon.

rfi.title: Israel formally recognises Armenian genocide in rebuke to Turkey
rfi.description: The Israeli government on Sunday unanimously recognised the massacres of Armenians during World War I as genocide, a move widely seen as a rebuke to Turkey and a stark signal of the deepening rift between the two countries.

rfi.title: France opens investigation after 11 killed in skydiving plane crash near Nancy
rfi.description: French investigators have begun examining the cause of a small aircraft crash near Nancy that killed 11 people, including private nurses making their first skydiving jump, in what officials say is the deadliest light aircraft accident recorded in France.

rfi.title: Macron hosts Oman sultan for talks on toll-free reopening of Strait of Hormuz
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron hosts Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq on Monday for the Gulf leader's first official visit to France, with talks expected to focus on securing the toll-free reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

rfi.title: France's deadly heatwave triggers accusations of government inaction
rfi.description: After 11 days of an exceptional heatwave and in the face of the heavy human toll that is beginning to emerge, politicians are accusing the French government of "incompetence" and "inaction." This comes after health officials said Sunday there had been around 1,000 more deaths than expected compared to previous months.

rfi.title: Why Germany is turning to Algeria for Europe's hydrogen future
rfi.description: Germany is strengthening its energy partnership with Algeria, as Europe searches for new long-term energy supplies and invests in renewable hydrogen to help cut emissions.

Up to 40 people have been arrested and 16 men, including high-ranking military officials, have been imprisoned across the country, according to local media.

The vessel, thought to have been carrying 10 people, did not issue a mayday call before sinking in the strait of Georgia

Police and rescue crews praised a couple who were passing in their yacht for making a critical mayday call and saving stranded passengers by pulling them onboard their craft.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : la communication de l’équipe de France sur une ligne de crête, entre « ambition » et « prétention »
lemonde.description: Entre des Bleus sûrs de leurs qualités, dont ils se targuent parfois, et leur sélectionneur, Didier Deschamps, adepte de la plus grande prudence en toutes circonstances, trouver le bon dosage n’est pas une tâche aisée.

lemonde.title: « Avec Donald Trump, le pari des Pères fondateurs sur l’exemplarité des présidents des Etats-Unis est perdu »
lemonde.description: Le président américain s’est extrait des contraintes morales qui pesaient sur ses prédécesseurs. Au moment où le pays s’apprête à célébrer les 250 ans de son indépendance, le pessimisme a gagné le pays, relève Gilles Paris, éditorialiste au « Monde », dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Kiev attaque à nouveau une raffinerie sur le sol russe, à 1 000 kilomètres de ses frontières, annonce Volodymyr Zelensky
lemonde.description: Les forces ukrainiennes ont frappé la principale raffinerie de pétrole d’Oufa pour la deuxième fois en une semaine, a déclaré le président ukrainien. Les autorités russes n’ont pas confirmé cette attaque.

lemonde.title: Canicule : la SNCF ne peut pas « garantir que tout va marcher très bien à 100 % » pour les départs en vacances
lemonde.description: La SNCF se prépare, a dit son président Jean Castex, à l’afflux de voyageurs dès vendredi, sans pouvoir garantir un fonctionnement normal en situation de canicule.

lemonde.title: Au Liban, la communauté chiite entre fierté et amertume face au Hezbollah, au deuil et à l’exil
lemonde.description: Au sortir d’une guerre dévastatrice, relancée en mars par le Parti de Dieu contre Israël, sympathisants et opposants de l’organisation s’interrogent sur le sens des sacrifices consentis alors qu’un accord-cadre a été signé le 26 juin entre le Liban et l’Etat hébreu.

lemonde.title: Victoria, 24 ans, actrice, entre 0 et 9 000 euros par mois : « Très vite, j’ai compris qu’il fallait choisir entre faire de l’art et faire de l’argent »
lemonde.description: « La bonne paye ». Chaque semaine, « Le Monde » parle d’argent avec les jeunes. Que signifie « bien gagner sa vie » ? Comment se projettent-ils dans l’avenir ? Cette semaine, Victoria raconte comment elle jongle entre les plateaux de tournage et de longues périodes d’incertitude.

lemonde.title: L’avocat Amar Bouaou, spécialisé dans la criminalité organisée, mis en examen pour « blanchiment en bande organisée » et « évasion fiscale »
lemonde.description: Le spécialiste de la procédure réputé a défendu de nombreuses figures de la criminalité organisée liée au trafic de stupéfiants. Ses avocats évoquent des « échanges de numéraires contre des virements » destinés à lui permettre de payer ses charges, « sans le moindre enrichissement ».

lemonde.title: Pour Edouard Philippe, ce serait « dangereux » si Gabriel Attal et lui se présentaient à la présidentielle 2027
lemonde.description: L’ancien premier ministre pointe un risque « d’élimination qui arriverait à ce cauchemar absolu, un deuxième tour avec Mme Le Pen ou M. Bardella face à M. Mélenchon ».

lemonde.title: « Nouvelle loi postale » : des députés dévoilent leurs, avec notamment la distribution du courrier quatre jours après son dépôt
lemonde.description: Un rapport parlementaire formule une quarantaine de mesures, dénonçant des « manquements multiples de l’Etat aux lourdes conséquences financières pour La Poste ».

lemonde.title: Affaire Luc Besson : la plaignante Sand Van Roy demande au ministère public de l’appuyer afin de rouvrir l’enquête pour viol
lemonde.description: La comédienne, dont l’avocat se prévaut d’une nouvelle analyse ADN, appelle le parquet général de Paris à lui aussi se pourvoir face à Luc Besson. Le réalisateur et producteur a bénéficié dans cette affaire d’un non-lieu, confirmé en appel puis en cassation en 2023.

lemonde.title: Mon master : le désarroi des candidats de la filière psychologie
lemonde.description: Seul un diplômé de licence sur deux parvient à intégrer un cursus dans ce domaine, faute de places. Un paradoxe alors que le gouvernement a prolongé en 2026 la « grande cause nationale » consacrée à la santé mentale.

lemonde.title: Isabelle Adjani condamnée en appel à une peine réduite à dix mois de prison avec sursis pour fraude fiscale aggravée
lemonde.description: L’artiste de 71 ans avait été condamnée en première instance à deux ans d’emprisonnement avec sursis et 250 000 euros d’amende, notamment pour s’être fictivement domiciliée au Portugal en 2016 et en 2017. Elle a annoncé se pourvoir en cassation.

lemonde.title: « Les étrangers dehors ! » : en Afrique du Sud, les mouvements xénophobes réussissent leur démonstration de force
lemonde.description: Mardi 30 juin, des manifestations contre les étrangers en situation irrégulière à l’appel du mouvement March and March se sont tenues dans les grandes villes. Des violences étaient redoutées, mais la journée s’est globalement déroulée dans le calme.

lemonde.title: Congé supplémentaire de naissance : comment fonctionne le nouveau disposif
lemonde.description: Le nouveau congé supplémentaire de naissance entre en vigueur à compter du 1er juillet. Qui y a droit ? Quand faut-il prévenir son employeur ? Comment l’indemnité sera-t-elle calculée ? Les Décodeurs passent en revue les principales questions qui se posent.

lemonde.title: Au festival d’Aix-en-Provence, entre la chaleur et les problèmes de son, l’opéra au défi du plein air
lemonde.description: Orage, vent, soleil, absence de réverbération… Face aux contraintes du Théâtre de l’Archevêché, le festival d’art lyrique utilise la technologie afin de rendre l’expérience plus confortable, pour le public comme pour les musiciens.

lemonde.title: Savez-vous ce qui émet un peu ou beaucoup de CO₂ : prendre l’avion, manger de la viande ou utiliser un sèche-linge pendant un an ?
lemonde.description: Alimentation, transports, logement, chauffage, achats d’équipement ou du quotidien… Testez vos connaissances des ordres de grandeur avec notre quiz.

france24fr.title: Le ministère de la Santé a-t-il publié un guide officiel expliquant "comment boire de l'eau" ?
france24fr.description: Présentée comme un guide officiel du ministère de la Santé expliquant "comment boire de l'eau", une affiche est devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux pendant la canicule en France. C'est en réalité une parodie qui détourne les codes de la communication institutionnelle et alimente un discours dénonçant une supposée "infantilisation" des citoyens.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : allégresse au Mexique après la victoire contre l’Équateur
france24fr.description: Mercredi, des foules immenses se sont rassemblées dans les rues des grandes villes mexicaines pour célébrer la victoire 2-0 du pays face à l'Équateur en Coupe du Monde. Cette victoire est la première du Mexique dans un match à élimination directe de la Coupe du monde depuis 1986.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : passe d'armes entre le gourvernement et les écologistes
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre et les Ecologistes ont bataillé mardi à l'Assemblée nationale sur les décès dus à la canicule et la politique d'adaptation du gouvernement face au changement climatique, les députés verts annonçant le dépôt d'une motion de censure.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le récital des Bleus
france24fr.description: Auteur d'un doublé sensationnel, Kylian Mbappé a percé le verrou suédois (3-0) mardi pour envoyer la France en 8es de finale de la Coupe du monde, où l'attend le Paraguay, tombeur surprenant de l'Allemagne, dans un remake inattendu du Mondial 1998.

france24fr.title: Au Brésil, les stigmates du Mondial 2014 : quand le football devient politique
france24fr.description: Le Brésil sera bien en huitièmes de finale du Mondial de football 2026. Pourtant, de nombreux spécialistes avaient prédit que le Japon allait avoir raison de la Seleção en 16es de finale. Le Brésil – pays du foot qui a toujours fait rêver – perdait un peu de sa superbe au fil des Coupes du monde depuis la débâcle contre l'Allemagne (7-1) en 2014 à domicile, un Mondial qui a traumatisé le pays et pas seulement à cause de la défaite.

france24fr.title: "Colère", "stratégie du chaos" : pourquoi les dates de la présidentielle française divisent
france24fr.description: La date du second tour de la présidentielle française, le 2 mai, suscite les critiques à droite comme à gauche. Bruno Retailleau dénonce un vote, au lendemain de la Fête du travail, avantageux pour la gauche. Des débordements durant les manifestations pourraient, au contraire, favoriser la droite.

france24fr.title: Les Écologistes annoncent "10 000 morts de la canicule", colère de Sébastien Lecornu
france24fr.description: Les Écologistes accusent le gouvernement "d'impréparation" et avancent le chiffre de 10 000 morts de la vague de chaleur. Les Verts pointent du doigt la responsabilité des autorités. Des propos qui ont provoqué la colère du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, alors que les chiffres des décès liés à la canicule seront connus dans quelques semaines selon Santé Publique France. Les Écologistes ont déposé une motion de censure contre le gouvernement.

france24fr.title: Violences sexuelles sur les enfants : Lecornu réduit le délai d'enquête et confirme la perpétuité
france24fr.description: Une "lettre rectificative" au projet de loi sur la protection des mineurs a été présentée mercredi en Conseil des ministres par le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu. Celle-ci vise à "fixer un délai maximal de trois mois" à la réalisation des enquêtes pour crimes sexuels sur des enfants, qui pourront également donner lieu à "la perpétuité".

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud: le rêve arc-en-ciel à l'épreuve? Avec T. Vircoulon, D. Delos, C. Dumay et M. Gbaffou
france24fr.description: En Afrique du Sud, une vague de violences xénophobes tournée principalement vers les immigrés clandestins subsahariens déferle depuis plusieurs semaines. La journée d'hier a été le point d'orgue d'une campagne lancée par des groupes qui se disent citoyens, dont le discours a déjà provoqué la mort de quatre personnes et qui a suscité l'exil forcé de 25 000 autres. Est-ce à dire que l'arc-en-ciel sud-africain a perdu de ses couleurs 35 ans après la fin de l'apartheid ?

france24fr.title: France 24 à la rencontre des sinistrés du double séisme au Venezuela
france24fr.description: Au Venezuela, des milliers de personnes recherchent leur proches dans les décombres du séisme qui a frappé le pays il y a une semaine. "Je cherche mon père, qu'il soit vivant ou mort"... France 24 est allé à leur rencontre.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Michael Olise, nouvelle star de l'équipe de France ?
france24fr.description: Lors de la victoire des Bleus en 16es de finale contre la Suède, l'attaquant Michael Olise a brillé. Dans toutes les bonnes actions, le joueur du Bayern Munich a éclaboussé la rencontre de son talent. En quelques semaines, il est devenu la nouvelle pépite de la sélection nationale.

france24fr.title: Face à la solitude, la Chine mise sur un compagnon androïde à 15 500 euros

france24fr.title: Environnement : les océans mondiaux ont atteint un pic de chaleur en juin
france24fr.description: Les océans ont enregistré leur mois de juin le plus chaud jamais observé. Avec une température moyenne à la surface des océans de 20,98°C en juin,  elle bat le précédent record établi en juin 2024 (20,89°C). Le premier semestre 2026 dans son ensemble est le deuxième plus chaud jamais enregistré, juste derrière les six premiers mois de 2024.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela : à La Guaira, la recherche des morts et des survivants continue
france24fr.description: Après les séismes meurtrier au Vénézuela, la population et les secouristes se mobilisent pour retrouver morts et survivants. À La Guaira, les habitants fouillent les décombres à la recherche de leurs proches.

france24fr.title: Poussant en zone contaminée, le miscanthus géant testé en Ukraine pour dépolluer les sols
france24fr.description: Connu pour ses vertus énergétiques, le miscanthus géant est testé depuis 2023 en Ukraine pour revitaliser les sols contaminés en raison de la guerre. Le projet, parrainé par l'Otan et piloté par une université tchèque, vise à vérifier la capacité de cette plante originaire d'Asie à absorber les polluants et à capter et stocker le carbone.

france24fr.title: Petits colis : l'Europe taxe Temu, Shein et consorts
france24fr.description: La nouvelle taxe européenne sur les petits colis importés est entrée en vigueur ce 1er juillet. Fixée à 3 euros par type d'article, elle remplace l'exemption de droits de douane qui bénéficiait jusqu'ici aux envois de moins de 150 euros. La France, qui avait instauré sa propre taxe de 2 euros en mars devant s'ajouter à la taxe européenne, a finalement décidé de l'abandonner.

new-sci.title: Humans sleep the least of all apes – is it the secret to our success?
new-sci.description: Sleep is essential, yet humans have evolved to need so little of it. When evolutionary anthropologist David Samson delved into our ancient past to find the reasons why, he discovered surprising ways to get a better night’s rest

new-sci.title: Your menstrual cycle may affect how well vaccines work
new-sci.description: Women who were vaccinated against covid-19 in the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle reported having a breakthrough infection sooner than those vaccinated during their follicular phase

new-sci.title: Remote-controlled cockroach swarm can now breathe underwater
new-sci.description: Tiny 3D-printed diving suits allow cockroaches to walk underwater for up to 3 hours with no ill effects, which could enable a cyborg insect swarm to explore disaster zones and perhaps even Mars

new-sci.title: Neuroscience can't tell us the way to govern people's brains
new-sci.description: From the age of legal adulthood to the concept of "profound autism", policy-makers are turning to neuroscience to help shape laws and policies, but the science simply isn't ready

new-sci.title: Ancient human DNA found on cave art for the first time
new-sci.description: DNA from ancient humans has been found on a prehistoric cave painting and on cave walls, demonstrating the potential to one day identify individual artists and resolve the debate over Neanderthals' artistic abilities

new-sci.title: Where, when and how to watch the 2026 solar eclipse
new-sci.description: This August a total solar eclipse is set to be visible across parts of Europe, while a partial eclipse will sweep across about a quarter of the planet – here’s how to catch it

new-sci.title: The race to understand how and when Thwaites glacier will collapse
new-sci.description: The loss of Antarctica’s doomsday glacier would transform our planet. Now scientists are revealing the secrets of this remotest of places, and asking the question: is its demise inevitable?

new-sci.title: How menopause radically changes the brain – and what happens after
new-sci.description: The brain undergoes a full renovation during menopause. Although these changes are profound, we’re learning that the long-term impact needn’t be all bad

new-sci.title: Parenting may permanently improve brain health for mums and dads
new-sci.description: Raising children appears to keep the brain young, potentially acting as a buffer against cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s

phys-org.title: Video: Thousands of planets are hidden in this image
phys-org.description: Millions of stars. Thousands of hidden worlds. One unprecedented view of our galaxy. Three years since launch, ESA's Euclid space telescope reveals the center of the Milky Way galaxy in extraordinary detail: a mosaic of tens of millions of stars captured in just 26 hours. But this is more than an image. It is a map of stellar evolution, from dark clouds where stars are being born to ancient populations packed into the galactic bulge.

phys-org.title: Woodcock charge deer to defend nests, footage reveals
phys-org.description: American woodcock, short, plump shorebirds with long, thin beaks, are widely known for their bobbing stride and nasally "peent" calls, but not for being aggressive. Yet one April afternoon, when a deer sniffed around a woodcock hen's ground nest looking for food, the hen lunged at it, scaring it away.

phys-org.title: 400-year-old painting reveals a bat's secret diet
phys-org.description: Natural historians have many observational techniques in their toolkit for learning about the natural world: tagging animals with tracking devices, recording sounds, analyzing droppings or simply watching and counting. As technology has advanced, these methods have grown far more precise and wide-reaching, letting researchers capture details that were once impossible to detect. Even today, however, these cutting-edge tools aren't the only route to discovery.

phys-org.title: Are you 'happee' or are you 'happeh?' Study links accents to social classes
phys-org.description: Our accents give away more about social class than we think, according to new research led by Lancaster University. The new sociolinguistic study focusing on Mancunian accents, published in the journal, Language Variation and Change, shows that the final vowel in words like happy, baby, chilly and city—known to linguists as "the happy vowel"—varies clearly by social class across Manchester.

phys-org.title: Mismatched work–life boundaries while working from home can push couples toward breaking up
phys-org.description: The COVID-19 pandemic transformed the way people work, making remote and work-from-home (WFH) jobs far more common than ever before. Even after social distancing ended, many companies and employees chose to stick with this model because it offers greater flexibility. People can work from where they already live, avoid long commutes, and enjoy a better work-life balance. For primary caregivers in particular, remote work has made it easier to juggle professional and personal responsibilities. A re

phys-org.title: What made trees possible? New research points to drought
phys-org.description: A study is reframing a fundamental question in plant evolution: What made trees possible? Researchers from Cal Poly Humboldt, Yale University, the University of Hohenheim in Germany and the Czech Academy of Sciences set out to understand how trees evolved and what allowed them to become some of the largest and longest-living organisms on Earth.

phys-org.title: Were Clovis foragers in Late Pleistocene North America big-game hunters, or just big-game scavengers?
phys-org.description: There are currently 15 well-documented Late Pleistocene localities in North America in which Clovis points are found associated with proboscidean remains (of mammoth, mastodon and gomphothere). Archaeologists routinely assume these localities represent evidence that Clovis people hunted these multi-ton animals, and in turn invoke that evidence to claim humans had a role in the extinction of these large mammals.

phys-org.title: Why taking a sick day depends on more than being sick
phys-org.description: As winter illness spreads and households face cost-of-living pressure, many Australians cannot treat a sick day as a simple health decision. They may be too sick to work—but their job is too insecure to stay home. New research led by UTS shows the decision to take sick leave is heavily influenced by pay, job security and gender.

phys-org.title: Webb reveals merger scars in galaxies that stopped forming stars 9 billion years ago
phys-org.description: Research has shed new light on why some distant galaxies suddenly stop forming stars. An international team led by astronomers at the University of Nottingham has used the James Webb Space Telescope to study a large sample of recently "quenched" galaxies in the distant universe, observed around nine billion years ago. Their findings appear in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

phys-org.title: Helping children navigate the emotional aftershocks of an earthquake
phys-org.description: The devastating earthquake in Venezuela has left countless families grieving, displaced and searching for loved ones. For many South Florida families with ties to the region, the tragedy feels especially close to home.

phys-org.title: Galaxy groups hiding in the universe's emptiest places
phys-org.description: Imagine standing in the emptiest place the universe has to offer, a stretch of cosmic ocean so vast that light takes tens of millions of years to cross it, and yet still finding company. That is the puzzle behind a new study built on the Calar Alto Void Integral field Treasury surveY, or CAVITY, posted to the arXiv preprint server.

phys-org.title: Darwin residents want answers on toxic gas emissions: Science shows their concerns are warranted
phys-org.description: For years, Darwin residents have been concerned about toxic chemicals emitted by the city's two gas export facilities. In fact, some locals are so worried about these airborne chemicals—particularly benzene—they recently formed a community group and launched a fundraiser to buy a regulation-grade mobile device for continuous monitoring.

phys-org.title: Himalayan pangolin emerges as distinct species, confirmed with DNA from 19th-century specimen
phys-org.description: The pangolin is a midsize mammal found only in Africa and Asia. The pangolins' scales make them unique, but these scales have become their undoing. Pangolins are poached for their scales, making them the most highly trafficked mammals in the world and, consequently, at high risk of extinction.

phys-org.title: Polymer network reconfigures in sequence, helping elastomers stay tough under strain
phys-org.description: Shock-absorbing sneaker soles are likely made of polyurethane, a highly elastic and tough polymer. The ability of these elastomers to absorb impact without breaking is extremely important for practical applications. While multiple strategies exist for enhancing elastomer toughness, each has its limitations. However, achieving synergistic toughening by integrating all three mechanisms within a single material remains challenging.

phys-org.title: NASA rolls out three robotic moon missions as 2029 lunar base plans take shape
phys-org.description: NASA on Tuesday announced new uncrewed missions to aid in the future creation of a lunar surface base, a project beginning to take shape despite recent setbacks.

phys-org.title: World's oceans break June heat record: EU monitor
phys-org.description: The world's oceans just experienced their hottest June on record and could set fresh highs in the months ahead as El Nino and climate change drive temperatures even higher, scientists said Wednesday.

phys-org.title: NASA vows to send ball to the moon if US wins World Cup
phys-org.description: NASA's chief on Tuesday tried to rally Team U.S. players in this year's World Cup tournament, promising to send a soccer ball to the moon if they win it all.

phys-org.title: Italy displays paintings from an ancient Etruscan tomb, its latest cultural acquisition
phys-org.description: Italy on Tuesday put on display one of the best known examples of Etruscan painting, panels from a tomb that it acquired for 15 million euros ($17 million) in the Culture Ministry's buying spree of big-ticket pieces of the country's cultural heritage.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

proj-syn.description: Around the world, childhood is being reprogrammed by digital technologies that shape how young people learn, play, and connect. But children and young people are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity, which is why we must shape digital environments that protect and support their healthy development.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy’s Ancient Origins

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Trap
proj-syn.description: Policymakers obsessed with competitiveness both in Europe and beyond need to abandon old orthodoxies. New research finds that for two decades, capital in Europe has been abundant and cheap, and corporate profits strong, yet investment, productivity, and wages have stalled, and labor's share of total income has shrunk.

proj-syn.title: How to Empower Africa’s Multilateral Development Banks
proj-syn.description: Capitalizing multilateral development banks in Africa is a strategic investment in the continent’s economic transformation. To mobilize adequate funding will require leveraging domestic savings, pursuing monetary integration, using innovative financing mechanisms, and strengthening regional capital markets.

proj-syn.title: Why Americans Are Wary of AI
proj-syn.description: The tech industry is asking Americans to embrace AI at a moment when trust in government is declining. While these may seem like separate issues, persuading people to trust AI will be far more difficult if they do not trust the institutions responsible for regulating it.

proj-syn.title: Why the Gulf Needs Economic Ties with Iran
proj-syn.description: Most Gulf observers agree that the old security order is dying. But none of the most commonly proposed options—buying more advanced weapons, seeking protection from new partners in the Global South, or building stronger national militaries—is sufficient on its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Tackle Developing Countries’ Cancer Crisis
proj-syn.description: Some health advocates believe that weakening intellectual-property protections and capping prices for the most advanced cancer treatments would expand access in developing countries. But this well-intentioned argument overlooks an inescapable reality: without strong incentives for innovation, such treatments would not exist.

proj-syn.title: Enforce AI Guardrails Before It’s Too Late
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration’s decision to impose export controls on Anthropic’s latest models is emblematic of the incoherent and shifting response from policymakers worldwide to the rapidly advancing AI sector. To ensure that these tools do not court disaster, governments must establish meaningful guardrails.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.
